questions.question: If A's salary is 16% more than that of B, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required percentage = [r ÷ (100 + r)] × 100

Given **r = 16%**

Required % = [16 ÷ (100 + 16)] × 100

Required % = [16 ÷ 116] × 100 = 400 ÷ 29 ≈ 13.79%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.79%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e20661ec35cbd3bf53a8b2be815e0befa91e0a57dbc310ad6a0955b38fce60b5.png] 

**Given:**

**A's salary** is 16% more than **B's salary**.

⇒ Let **B's salary** = 100

⇒ **A's salary** = 100 + 16% of 100 = 116

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference between **A** and **B** = 116 − 100 = 16

⇒ **B's salary** is less than **A's salary** by = (Difference ÷ A's salary) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (16 ÷ 116) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (4 ÷ 29) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = 400 ÷ 29 = 13.7931...

⇒ Correct to two decimal places = 13.79%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.79%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison Rule

If A is **r% more** than B, then B is **[r ÷ (100 + r)] × 100%** less than A.

Inverse Case

If A is **r% less** than B, then B is **[r ÷ (100 − r)] × 100%** more than A.

Base Value Concept

The percentage change depends on the **denominator (base value)**. When comparing B to A, **A's value** becomes the base.</p

questions.question: 15 chairs and 19 tables cost ₹5,300 and 19 chairs and 19 tables cost ₹5,700. What is the cost of 12 chairs and 13 tables?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the two scenarios: (19 chairs + 19 tables) − (15 chairs + 19 tables) = ₹5,700 − ₹5,300.

This gives 4 **chairs** = ₹400 ⇒ Cost of 1 **chair** = ₹100.

From the second set: 19 **tables** = 5,700 − (19 × 100) = ₹3,800 ⇒ Cost of 1 **table** = ₹200.

Required cost for 12 **chairs** and 13 **tables** = (12 × 100) + (13 × 200) = 1,200 + 2,600 = ₹3,800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,800.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 15 chairs and 19 tables = ₹5,300

Cost of 19 chairs and 19 tables = ₹5,700

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost = (Number of chairs × Price per chair) + (Number of tables × Price per table)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d92dc91ab38a3fc8d7e630316c9a985dec811b83f736c670189687f152f44686.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let C be the cost of one **chair** and T be the cost of one **table**.

⇒ 15C + 19T = 5300 — (Eq. 1)

⇒ 19C + 19T = 5700 — (Eq. 2)

⇒ Subtracting Eq. 1 from Eq. 2:

⇒ (19C − 15C) + (19T − 19T) = 5700 − 5300

⇒ 4C = 400

⇒ C = 100

⇒ Substitute C = 100 in Eq. 2:

⇒ 19(100) + 19T = 5700

⇒ 1900 + 19T = 5700

⇒ 19T = 5700 − 1900 = 3800

⇒ T = 3800 ÷ 19 = 200

⇒ Cost of 12 chairs and 13 tables = 12C + 13T

⇒ Cost = 12(100) + 13(200) = 1200 + 2600 = 3800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,800.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simultaneous Linear Equations

Equations with two variables can be solved using the **elimination method** (removing one variable) or the **substitution method**.

Unitary Method

Finding the value of a **single unit** first helps in calculating the value of any required number of units easily.

Total Cost Formula

Total Cost = ∑ (Rateᵢ × Quantityᵢ). For multiple items, sum the individual costs of each item category.

__

• As per the **Ministry of Finance**, the **SGST (State Goods and Services Tax)** revenue, including compensation to states, has consistently demonstrated a buoyancy above 1 in the post-GST period from **2017-18 to 2022-23**.

__
 
• **Zero**__

 __

• This scenario is unlikely for GST, as the tax reform has been designed to improve compliance and revenue collection.

 __

questions.question: If a : b :: b : c, c = 9a and b = 6, then find the positive value of c.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **a, b, c** are in **continued proportion** (a : b :: b : c).

The relation is **b² = ac**.

Substitute **b = 6** and **c = 9a** (so **a = c/9**).

6² = (c/9) × c ⇒ 36 = c² / 9 ⇒ c² = 324 ⇒ c = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Proportion: **a : b :: b : c**

Values: **b = 6**, **c = 9a**

**Formula Used:**

For continued proportion, **Product of extremes = Product of means** ⇒ **ac = b²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d63bc6a3eb1962bee536a999d590ae6787b246d2422afee54129f24c6359a124.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ a/b = b/c

⇒ b² = a × c

⇒ Substitute c = 9a → a = c/9

⇒ 6² = (c/9) × c

⇒ 36 = c² / 9

⇒ c² = 36 × 9

⇒ c² = 324

⇒ c = √324

⇒ c = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

**__Additional Information__**

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c. Here, b is called the **mean proportional** between a and c.

Mean Proportional Formula

The mean proportional **b** between two numbers **a** and **c** is calculated as **b = √(ac)**.

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, the term **c** is known as the **third proportional** to a and b, where **c = b²/a**.</p

questions.question: In what time (in years) will ₹2,500 fetch an interest of ₹1,000 at 10% per year simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 1 year = 10% of **₹2,500** = **₹250**

Total interest to be fetched = **₹1,000**

**Time** = Total Interest ÷ Interest per year

⇒ **Time** = 1000 ÷ 250 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,500

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹1,000

**Rate (R)** = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c145dd59f81b4564a611278147ec8ec41980e034b373221e61e1a4926789b1d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1000 = (2500 × 10 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1000 = 250 × T

⇒ T = 1000 ÷ 250

⇒ T = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

Amount (A) is the sum of Principal (P) and Interest (I). Formula: A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100 or A = P(1 + RT/100).

Compound Interest (CI) vs Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas CI is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes to double your money: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate (usually applied to Compound Interest).

questions.question: A boat takes 27 minutes to go 37.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat instill water to that of the stream is 8 : 5. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 79.4 km upstream and 85.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Upstream speed** (U) = 37.2 km / (27/60) h = 82.67 kmph

Ratio **Boat** : **Stream** = 8 : 5 → **Upstream ratio** = 8 − 5 = 3 units; **Downstream ratio** = 8 + 5 = 13 units.

3 units = 82.66 kmph ⇒ 1 unit = 27.55 kmph ⇒ Downstream (13 units) = 358.22 kmph.

Total Time = (79.4 / 82.66) + (85.8 / 358.22) ≈ 0.96 + 0.24 = 1.2 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bb5b09ee316b50a36e61f1327c45fac86ad93f23c873ed057a1340a6a4987b8.png] 

**Given:** Upstream Distance = 37.2 km, Time = 27 min, Ratio of Boat speed (v) to Stream speed (u) = 8 : 5.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Upstream Speed (U) = v − u | Downstream Speed (D) = v + u.

⇒ U = 37.2 ÷ (27/60) = (37.2 × 60) ÷ 27 = 2232 ÷ 27 = 82.666... kmph.

⇒ Let v = 8x and u = 5x. Then U = 8x − 5x = 3x.

⇒ 3x = 82.666... ⇒ x = 27.555... kmph.

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 8x + 5x = 13x = 13 × 27.555... = 358.222... kmph.

⇒ Time for 79.4 km upstream = 79.4 ÷ 82.666... = 0.9605 hours.

⇒ Time for 85.8 km downstream = 85.8 ÷ 358.222... = 0.2395 hours.

⇒ Total Time = 0.9605 + 0.2395 = 1.2 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Water

Upstream speed is the difference (v − u) and Downstream speed is the sum (v + u) of the boat and stream speeds.

Conversion of Time

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To calculate speed in kmph, distance in km must be divided by time in hours.

Boat Speed Calculation

Speed of boat in still water (v) = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2 and Stream speed (u) = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2.</p

For **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

questions.question: Which of the following best encapsulates the concept of a 'stored-program computer'as introduced by the Von Neumann architecture?

options.text: A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry
A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution
A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution
A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Von Neumann architecture** introduced the concept of a stored-program computer.
 
• In this architecture, both **data and instructions** are stored together in the same memory unit, enabling the processor to access them sequentially.
 
• This design uses a single memory space for storing both **programs (instructions)** and **data**, eliminating the need for separate storage units.
 
• The stored-program concept allows flexibility, enabling computers to execute different programs without hardware modifications.
 
• The architecture consists of key components such as a **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **memory**, and **I/O devices**.
 
• The CPU executes instructions sequentially, fetching them from memory, decoding them, and performing operations as specified.
 
• This model laid the foundation for modern computing systems and is used in almost all general-purpose computers today.
 
• The concept revolutionized computing by introducing programmability and reducing dependency on external hardware for processing instructions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry**__

 __
 
• This describes an **early computing model**, such as those used in the pre-Von Neumann era.
 
• These systems, often referred to as **hardwired computers**, lacked flexibility and required physical rewiring to change instructions.
 
 
 
• **A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution**__
 __
 
• This describes systems that depend heavily on **external media** such as tapes or disks for program storage and execution.
 
• Such systems are less efficient compared to the stored-program model introduced by Von Neumann.
 
 
 
• **A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed**__
 
 
• This describes the **Harvard architecture**, which is distinct from the Von Neumann model.
 
• In the Harvard architecture, separate memory units for data and instructions enable parallel access, improving processing speed.

questions.question:
Simplify:

(cot theta)/(operatorname{cosec) theta+1}+frac{operatorname{cosec} theta+1}{cot theta}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put **θ = 30°** in the given expression.

cot 30° = √3 and cosec 30° = 2.

Expression = [√3 / (2 + 1)] + [(2 + 1) / √3] = [√3 / 3] + [3 / √3] = [1 / √3] + √3 = (1 + 3) / √3 = 4 / √3.

Check options for θ = 30°: 2sec 30° = 2 × (2 / √3) = 4 / √3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2secθ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [cot θ / (cosec θ + 1)] + [(cosec θ + 1) / cot θ]

**Formula Used:** cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 ⇒ cot²θ = cosec²θ − 1 = (cosec θ + 1)(cosec θ − 1)

⇒ Taking LCM: [cot²θ + (cosec θ + 1)²] / [cot θ(cosec θ + 1)]

⇒ [cot²θ + cosec²θ + 1 + 2cosec θ] / [cot θ(cosec θ + 1)]

⇒ [(cosec²θ − 1) + cosec²θ + 1 + 2cosec θ] / [cot θ(cosec θ + 1)]

⇒ [2cosec²θ + 2cosec θ] / [cot θ(cosec θ + 1)]

⇒ [2cosec θ (cosec θ + 1)] / [cot θ (cosec θ + 1)]

⇒ 2cosec θ / cot θ = 2(1 / sin θ) / (cos θ / sin θ)

⇒ 2 / cos θ = 2sec θ

**∴ The correct answer is 2secθ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard Pythagorean identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.</p

questions.question: The shorter side of a rectangle is 21 cm less than the longer side. The numerical value of its area is equal to 7 times the numerical value of its perimeter. What is the length (in cm) of its longer side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **longer side** be L. Then the **shorter side** is L − 21.

Area = 7 × Perimeter ⇒ L × (L − 21) = 7 × 2 × [L + (L − 21)]

L² − 21L = 14(2L − 21) ⇒ L² − 21L = 28L − 294

L² − 49L + 294 = 0. Solving this: (L − 42)(L − 7) = 0.

Since L > 21, the only possible value for the **longer side** is 42 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b4bba9c35121a366a4effa2e087f6b4c3296c0fdb955b6e428d1bd638f84c1a.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Let **Longer side** = x cm

⇒ **Shorter side** = (x − 21) cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Area of Rectangle** = Length × Breadth

⇒ **Perimeter of Rectangle** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 7 × Perimeter

⇒ x(x − 21) = 7 × 2[x + (x − 21)]

⇒ x² − 21x = 14(2x − 21)

⇒ x² − 21x = 28x − 294

⇒ x² − 49x + 294 = 0

⇒ x² − 42x − 7x + 294 = 0

⇒ x(x − 42) − 7(x − 42) = 0

⇒ (x − 42)(x − 7) = 0

⇒ x = 42 or x = 7

⇒ Since the side must be greater than 21 (as x − 21 must be positive), x = 42 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Diagonals are equal and bisect each other.

Diagonal Formula

The length of the diagonal (d) of a rectangle is given by d = √(L² + B²).

Quadratic Root Selection

In geometry word problems, always check if the calculated side length makes all other dimensions (like L − 21) positive real numbers.</p

questions.question: If a² + b² = 90 and ab = 27, then find the possible value of(a+b)/(a-b)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Required value = √[(Sum of squares + 2 × Product) ÷ (Sum of squares − 2 × Product)]

Ratio = √[(90 + 2 × 27) ÷ (90 − 2 × 27)]

Ratio = √[144 ÷ 36] = 12 ÷ 6 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **a² + b² = 90**

⇒ **ab = 27**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

⇒ **(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab**

⇒ (a + b)² = 90 + 2(27) = 144

⇒ a + b = √144 = 12

⇒ (a − b)² = 90 − 2(27) = 36

⇒ a − b = √36 = 6

⇒ Required fraction = (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = 12 ÷ 6 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for 4ab

The relationship between the square of the sum and the square of the difference is given by (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Sum of Squares

The sum of squares a² + b² can be expressed as ((a + b)² + (a − b)²) ÷ 2.

Difference of Squares

The product of the sum and difference of two numbers results in the difference of their squares: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².</p

questions.question: Find the roots of the quadratic equation 5x² - 12x - 17 = 0
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For the equation 5x² − 12x − 17 = 0, find two numbers that multiply to (5 × −17) = −85 and add to −12.

The numbers are −17 and +5.

The roots are obtained by changing the signs of these numbers and dividing by the coefficient of x² (a = 5).

Roots = −(−17)/5 and −(5)/5 ⇒ 17/5 and −1.

**∴ The correct answer is -1, 17/5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** 5x² − 12x − 17 = 0

**Method:** Factorization by splitting the middle term

⇒ 5x² − 17x + 5x − 17 = 0

⇒ x(5x − 17) + 1(5x − 17) = 0

⇒ (5x − 17)(x + 1) = 0

Now, set each factor equal to zero:

⇒ 5x − 17 = 0 ⇒ 5x = 17 ⇒ x = 17/5

⇒ x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = −1

The roots of the equation are −1 and 17/5.

**∴ The correct answer is -1, 17/5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The discriminant D is given by b² − 4ac. Since D = (−12)² − 4(5)(−17) = 144 + 340 = 484 > 0, the roots are real and distinct.

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, sum of roots = −b/a and product of roots = c/a. Here, sum = 12/5 and product = −17/5.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can also be found using x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.</p

• Certain types of RNA, such as **ribozymes**, exhibit **catalytic functions**. Ribozymes catalyze biochemical reactions, such as cleaving RNA molecules or forming peptide bonds during protein synthesis.
 
• The discovery of catalytic RNA challenged the traditional belief that only **proteins** could act as enzymes.
 
• RNA is involved in processes such as **gene regulation, splicing, and editing**, highlighting its multifunctional nature.
 
• The ability of RNA to fold into complex three-dimensional structures is crucial for its catalytic and regulatory roles.

questions.question: The crest of a wave is the point where the disturbance is at:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **crest** of a wave is the point where the disturbance reaches its **maximum displacement** in an oscillatory motion.
 
• It is the **highest point** the wave reaches above its mean position or equilibrium line.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding **wave mechanics**, including water waves, sound waves, and electromagnetic waves.
 
• The crest is followed by the **trough**, which is the lowest point or the point of maximum negative displacement.
 
• In mathematical terms, for a sinusoidal wave, the crest corresponds to the point where the amplitude of the wave is at its **positive maximum value**.
 
• The concept of the crest is essential in various fields, including **physics, engineering, and oceanography**, as it helps in analyzing wave behavior, energy, and motion.
 
• Understanding the crest is crucial in determining the **wavelength** (distance between two consecutive crests) and the **frequency** of the wave.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Minimum point**__

 __
 
• The minimum point in a wave corresponds to the **trough**, which is the lowest point in the wave cycle or the point of maximum negative displacement.
 
• Troughs are essential for calculating the **amplitude** and determining the wave's energy.
 
 
 
• **Zero point**__
 __
 
• The zero point refers to the **mean position** or equilibrium line of the wave, where there is no displacement.
 
• It is the point of **zero disturbance** in the wave's cycle.
 
 
 
• **Constant point**__
 
 
• This term is not typically used in wave mechanics as waves are inherently oscillatory and do not remain constant.
 
• The motion of waves is characterized by continuous variations in displacement, making "constant point" an incorrect description.

questions.question: A student scored the following marks: 78, 85, 69, and 90 in four subjects. What score is required in the fifth subject to achieve an average of 80 marks across all five subjects?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Target **Average** = 80. Calculate **Net Deviation** of given marks from 80.

Deviations: (78−80) + (85−80) + (69−80) + (90−80) ⇒ −2 + 5 − 11 + 10 = +2.

To keep average at 80, **Net Deviation** must be 0. So, 5th subject deviation must be −2.

5th subject score = Target Average + Required Deviation ⇒ 80 + (−2) = 78.

**∴ The correct answer is 78 marks.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marks in 4 subjects = 78, 85, 69, 90; Required **Average** for 5 subjects = 80.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of Observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07c15cd6cd79fb63c81a89034765e974799c29a4cce4a1c214afea9b02a21757.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks required for 5 subjects = 80 × 5 = 400.

⇒ Sum of marks in 4 subjects = 78 + 85 + 69 + 90.

⇒ Sum of 4 subjects = 322.

⇒ Marks required in 5th subject = Total required marks − Current sum.

⇒ Marks in 5th subject = 400 − 322 = 78.

**∴ The correct answer is 78 marks.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean (μ) = Σx / n.

Net Deviation Rule

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is a powerful tool for solving missing value problems in averages.

New Observation Entry

New Observation = (New Average × New Count) − (Old Average × Old Count).</p

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 2 days. If A alone can do it in 38 days, then B alone can do 9-times of the same work in days.

Combined efficiency of **A + B** = 1/2 work/day

Efficiency of **A** = 1/38 work/day

Time for **B** to do 9-times work = (Total work × 9) ÷ Efficiency of B = 9 ÷ (9/19) = 19 days

**∴ The correct answer is 19 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A + B** = 2 days

Time taken by **A** alone = 38 days

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 19 − 1 = 18

⇒ Time taken by **B** = (9 × 38) ÷ 18

⇒ Time taken by **B** = 342 ÷ 18 = 19 days

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a work. If a person completes work in 'n' days, their 1-day work is 1/n.

If A takes 'x' days and B takes 'y' days, together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days to complete the **same work**.</p

questions.question: A motorist covers a distance of 30 km in 50 minutes by moving at a speed of x km/hr for the first 13 minutes, then moving at the speed of 2x km/hr for the next 25 minutes and then again moving at the speed of x km/hr for the rest of the journey. The value of x is equal to:

x = (30 × 60) ÷ 75 = 1800 ÷ 75 = 24 km/hr.

questions.question: The LCM of 48, 88 and another number, x, is 4752. Which of the following can be the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Prime Factorization** of given numbers:

48 = 2⁴ × 3¹

88 = 2³ × 11¹

**LCM** = 4752 = 2⁴ × 3³ × 11¹

Since the **LCM** has 3³, and neither 48 nor 88 contains 3³, **x** must be a multiple of 3³ (27). Only 216 is divisible by 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 48, 88, and **x**. **LCM** = 4752.

**Step 1:** Find the **prime factors** of the given numbers.

⇒ 48 = 16 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3¹

⇒ 88 = 8 × 11 = 2³ × 11¹

**Step 2:** Find the **prime factors** of the **LCM**.

⇒ 4752 = 2 × 2376 = 2² × 1188 = 2³ × 594 = 2⁴ × 297

⇒ 297 = 27 × 11 = 3³ × 11¹

⇒ **LCM** (48, 88, **x**) = 2⁴ × 3³ × 11¹

**Step 3:** Compare factors. **LCM** is the product of highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

⇒ Power of 2 in LCM is 2⁴ (comes from 48).

⇒ Power of 11 in LCM is 11¹ (comes from 88).

⇒ Power of 3 in LCM is 3³. However, 48 has only 3¹ and 88 has 3⁰.

⇒ Therefore, **x** must contain 3³ = 27 as a factor.

**Step 4:** Check options for multiples of 27.

⇒ 216 = 27 × 8 (Satisfies the condition).

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Definition

**Least Common Multiple** is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the numbers.

HCF vs LCM Relation

For two numbers **a** and **b**: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**. This does not directly apply to three numbers.

Divisibility Rule of 27

A number is divisible by 27 if the sum of its digits in blocks of three from right to left is divisible by 27.</p

questions.question: India's trade structure under British colonial rule was molded to serve the economic interests of Britain. Which of the following best describes India's trade structure at the eve of Independence?

options.text: Export of capital, import of labour

Export of industrial goods, import of food

• During the British colonial period, India's trade structure was designed to serve the **economic interests of Britain**.
 
• India became a supplier of **raw materials** such as cotton, jute, tea, and spices to Britain.
 
• At the same time, India was made a market for the import of **manufactured goods**, including textiles and machinery, from Britain.
 
• This unequal trade structure led to the decline of India's **indigenous industries**, including the famous textile industry.
 
• British policies ensured that India remained a **dependent economy** incapable of self-sustained industrial growth.
 
• The economic exploitation drained India's wealth and contributed significantly to the **poverty and backwardness** observed at the time of Independence.
 
• The combination of ** and manufactured goods imports** reinforced India's colonial subjugation and economic imbalance.
 
• This trade pattern is a classic example of colonial economic strategy focused on **resource extraction** and market monopolization.

questions.question: X varies inversely as Y and Y varies inversely as Z. In a particular ca X = (1)/(16) and Z = (1)/(32) What will be the value of X when Z = 3?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

X varies inversely as Y and Y varies inversely as Z.

Initial values: X = 1/16 and Z = 1/32.

New value: Z = 3.

**Formula Used:**

X × Y = k₁ (constant for X and Y).

Y × Z = k₂ (constant for Y and Z).

**Calculation:**

From X × Y = k₁ and Y × Z = k₂:

Y = k₁ / X, Z = k₂ / Y.

⇒ Z = k₂ / (k₁ / X).

⇒ Z = X × k₂ / k₁.

From the initial values, substitute X = 1/16 and Z = 1/32:

k₂ / k₁ = Z / X = (1/32) / (1/16).

k₂ / k₁ = 1/32 × 16/1 = 1/2.

Now, when Z = 3:

⇒ Z = X × k₂ / k₁.

⇒ 3 = X × (1/2).

⇒ X = 3 × 2.

⇒ X = 6.

**The value of X when Z = 3 is 6.**

questions.question: A (x, 5), B (3, -4) and C (-6, y) are the three vertices of a triangle ABC. If (3.5, 4.5) is the centroid of the triangle, find the point (x + 3, y - 4)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of x-coordinates = 3 × Centroidₓ ⇒ x + 3 − 6 = 3 × 3.5 = 10.5 ⇒ x = 13.5.

Sum of y-coordinates = 3 × Centroidy ⇒ 5 − 4 + y = 3 × 4.5 = 13.5 ⇒ y = 12.5.

Required point (x + 3, y − 4) = (13.5 + 3, 12.5 − 4) = (16.5, 8.5).

**∴ The correct answer is (16.5, 8.5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices of triangle are **A(x, 5)**, **B(3, −4)**, and **C(−6, y)**. The **centroid** is **G(3.5, 4.5)**.

**Formula Used:** Centroid G(X, Y) of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) is given by:

X = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃) / 3 and Y = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) / 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0e18447abea67554e2b6b9865013b02ad9669a1f7d4da83d0e561c8a03b006e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3.5 = (x + 3 + (−6)) / 3

⇒ 3.5 × 3 = x − 3

⇒ 10.5 = x − 3 ⇒ **x = 13.5**

⇒ 4.5 = (5 + (−4) + y) / 3

⇒ 4.5 × 3 = 1 + y

⇒ 13.5 = 1 + y ⇒ **y = 12.5**

⇒ Required point = (x + 3, y − 4)

⇒ Point = (13.5 + 3, 12.5 − 4)

⇒ Point = (16.5, 8.5)

**∴ The correct answer is (16.5, 8.5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Centroid Properties

The **centroid** is the intersection of the three **medians** and always lies inside the triangle. It divides each median in a **2:1 ratio**.

Area of Triangle (Coordinate Geometry)

Area = 0.5 × |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|. If the area is zero, the points are **collinear**.

Section Formula

A point dividing a line segment joining (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) in ratio m:n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m+n)).</p

questions.question: Under its original jurisdiction, the Supreme Court of India can adjudicate disputes between:

options.text: The Centre and one or more states
Two private citizens from different states
Two municipal corporations of different states
A state government and a private corporation

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Centre and one or more states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court of India is defined under **Article 131** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• In its original jurisdiction, the Supreme Court can adjudicate disputes between the **Government of India (Centre) and one or more states**.
 
• This jurisdiction is exclusive to the Supreme Court, meaning no other court in India can handle such disputes.
 
• It also includes disputes between **two or more states**, or between the Centre and any state(s) on one side and other states on the other side.
 
• This ensures the maintenance of a **federal balance** and resolves any legal conflicts that may arise between different levels of government.
 
• However, it is important to note that this jurisdiction is limited to **questions of law** or **questions of fact** on which the existence of a legal right depends.
 
• Some examples of cases under this jurisdiction include disputes related to **taxation, water disputes, or constitutional interpretation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Two private citizens from different states**__

 __
 
• Disputes between private citizens are not within the **original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court.
 
• Such matters are generally dealt with by **civil courts** or **high courts** in India.
 
 
 
• **Two municipal corporations of different states**__
 __
 
• Municipal corporations are governed by their respective state governments, and any disputes between them would not fall under the **original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court.
 
• Such cases would typically be resolved within the jurisdiction of the respective **state high courts**.
 
 
 
• **A state government and a private corporation**__
 
 
• Disputes involving private corporations are not covered under Article 131.
 
• Such matters are generally resolved through **civil courts** or other legal mechanisms, including tribunals.

questions.question: By how much is 60% of 40 greater than (2)/(5) of 55?

Find: (60% of 40) − (2/5 of 55)

Percentage: (p% of q) = (p × q) ÷ 100

Fraction: (m/n of q) = (m × q) ÷ n

**Calculations:**

⇒ 60% of 40 = (60 × 40) ÷ 100 = 2400 ÷ 100 = 24

⇒ Difference = 24 − 22 = 2

**∴ 60% of 40 is greater by 2.**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) in Indian tax regime.

1. MAT is calculated at 15% on the book profit or at the usual corporate rates, and whichever is lower is payable as tax.

2. Only domestic companies in India fall under this provision.

3. MAT is an important tool with which tax avoidance can be prevented.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT)** is a provision in the Indian tax regime aimed at ensuring that companies with substantial profits and paying little or no tax under normal provisions also contribute to the tax structure.
 
• MAT is calculated on the basis of **15% of the book profit** plus applicable surcharge and cess. However, the statement that it is levied at the lower of this rate or usual corporate rates is incorrect.
 
• MAT applies to **both domestic and foreign companies** (with specific exceptions), not just domestic companies. Hence, the second statement is incorrect.
 
• The third statement is correct as MAT serves as an **anti-tax-avoidance tool** by bringing companies under the tax net that would otherwise avoid taxes using exemptions, deductions, or incentives.
 
• MAT provisions are defined under **Section 115JB of the Income Tax Act, 1961**.
 
• Companies that are subject to MAT are required to pay the higher of the calculated MAT or the normal tax liability.
 
• MAT ensures a more equitable tax system by preventing companies from showing artificially reduced profits using accounting practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:**__

 __
 
• The claim that MAT is calculated at **15% or at the usual corporate rates, whichever is lower**, is factually incorrect. In practice, MAT is levied at a fixed rate of 15% of book profits (plus surcharge and cess, if applicable), and this is compared with the normal tax liability. The higher of the two is payable.
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:**__
 __
 
• MAT applies to **both domestic and foreign companies**, except for specific cases like companies in Special Economic Zones (SEZs) or those availing exemptions under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs).
 
• Foreign companies are subject to MAT if they have a presence in India and are required to prepare their profit and loss accounts under the Companies Act.
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:**__
 
 
• This is correct. MAT helps prevent **tax avoidance** by ensuring that companies with substantial book profits but reduced taxable income due to deductions and exemptions still pay a minimum amount of tax.
 
• It establishes a level playing field for companies by reducing the scope for aggressive tax planning.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge facing the development of inland waterways in India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Inland waterways** in India refer to the use of rivers, canals, backwaters, and lakes for the transportation of goods and passengers.
 
• The **absence of adequate terminal facilities** is a significant challenge in the development of inland waterways in India.
 
• Terminals are essential for loading, unloading, and storage of cargo as well as for the smooth functioning of water transportation.
 
• Lack of terminals creates bottlenecks in the system, affecting the **efficiency and cost-effectiveness** of waterway transportation.
 
• India has a vast network of rivers but many of them are not equipped with **modern terminal infrastructure**, leading to underutilization of this mode of transport.
 
• Government initiatives like the **Jal Marg Vikas Project (JMVP)** aim to address this challenge by improving infrastructure, including terminals, on National Waterways.
 
• Adequate terminal facilities are also necessary to ensure the **integration of waterways** with other modes of transportation like rail and road.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Minimal environmental concerns**__

 __
 
• Inland waterways are considered an **environmentally friendly** mode of transport as they produce lower emissions compared to road or rail transport.
 
• However, environmental concerns such as **impact on aquatic ecosystems**, water quality, and riverbank erosion must still be addressed.
 
 
 
• **High levels of private investment**__
 __
 
• Private investment in inland waterways has been **relatively low** due to the high initial cost and long gestation period of projects.
 
• Government support is often required to attract private players through **public-private partnerships (PPPs).**
 
 
 
• **Well-established infrastructure**__
 
 
• Contrary to the statement, the infrastructure for inland waterways in India is **still in the developmental stage**.
 
• Efforts like the development of **National Waterways** are ongoing to improve the infrastructure.

• The **Union Council of Ministers** in India consists of different levels of ministers, including the Prime Minister, **Cabinet Ministers**, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• A **Cabinet Minister** holds the highest position in the council after the Prime Minister and is responsible for major ministries such as Finance, Defence, Home Affairs, External Affairs, etc.
 
• Cabinet Ministers are part of the **core decision-making body** in the government and attend cabinet meetings chaired by the Prime Minister.
 
• The Cabinet Ministers are responsible for framing policies, implementing laws, and overseeing the functioning of their respective ministries.
 
• The hierarchy within the Union Council of Ministers places the **Cabinet Minister** immediately below the Prime Minister, followed by Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
 
• This structure ensures efficient governance and delegation of responsibilities across various levels of the government.
 
• Cabinet Ministers are appointed by the **President of India** on the advice of the Prime Minister.

• A **Minister of State** is a junior minister who assists the Cabinet Minister in handling their respective ministry.
 
• They may handle specific responsibilities within the ministry or act as independent ministers for less critical portfolios.
 
• While they attend meetings and contribute to policy discussions, they are not part of the core Cabinet meetings.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Minister**__
 __
 
• **Deputy Ministers** are at a lower rank compared to Ministers of State and mainly assist in administrative and operational tasks.
 
• They do not have independent portfolios and work under the guidance of senior ministers.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Secretary**__
 
 
• A **Parliamentary Secretary** is not considered a minister but acts as an aide to a senior minister or Cabinet Minister.
 
• They focus on legislative duties and help coordinate between the ministry and parliament.

questions.question: What is the nature of wavefront from a point source in an isotropic medium?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Spherical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **point source** emits light uniformly in all directions in an **isotropic medium**, where the medium has identical properties in every direction.
 
• The emitted light creates a wavefront that is equidistant from the point source at any given instant.
 
• The geometry of this wavefront is **spherical**, as it forms concentric spheres centered around the point source.
 
• Wavefronts are defined as surfaces of constant phase, and in the case of a point source, these surfaces expand radially outward, maintaining a spherical shape.
 
• The spherical wavefront is a fundamental concept in **optics** and is used to describe wave propagation in various applications.
 
• This behavior is explained by the **Huygens' Principle**, which states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets, propagating outward.
 
• The spherical nature of the wavefront is important in many fields, including **physics**, **acoustics**, and **engineering**, as it helps in understanding wave behavior in isotropic media.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Elliptical**__

 __
 
• An **elliptical wavefront** is associated with sources that emit waves in an anisotropic medium or when the propagation is affected by external factors such as direction-dependent properties of the medium.
 
• Elliptical wavefronts are less common in nature compared to spherical wavefronts.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical**__
 __
 
• **Cylindrical wavefronts** are generated by linear sources, such as a vibrating string or a slit in optics experiments.
 
• The wavefronts expand as concentric cylinders rather than spheres.
 
 
 
• **Plane**__
 
 
• **Plane wavefronts** occur when the source is very far away or when waves propagate in a single direction without divergence, such as lasers.
 
• In this case, the wavefronts appear as flat surfaces rather than curved ones.

questions.question: Which of the following movements, though initially religious in nature, later evolved into a peasant movement under the leadership of Dudu Miyan, son of Haji Shariatullah
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Farazi Movement** originated in Bengal in the early 19th century and was initially a **religious reform movement**.
 
• It was founded by **Haji Shariatullah**, who aimed to purify Islam by removing un-Islamic practices and emphasizing strict adherence to the Quran and Hadith.
 
• Under the leadership of **Dudu Miyan**, the son of Haji Shariatullah, the movement evolved into a **peasant movement**.
 
• Dudu Miyan mobilized the poor peasants against the oppressive **zamindars** (landowners) and moneylenders.
 
• The movement focused on **economic justice** and fought against the exploitation of peasants by landlords and British colonial administrators.
 
• It played a significant role in organizing the rural population and addressing their grievances, which made it an important socio-economic movement in Bengal.
 
• The Farazis were also known for their opposition to British rule and their efforts to resist colonial exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhill Uprising**__

 __
 
• The **Bhill Uprising** was a tribal revolt that occurred in the early 19th century in western India, particularly in the regions of **Khandesh** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• The Bhills, an indigenous tribe, revolted against the **British colonial administration** and local rulers due to exploitation and loss of their traditional lands.
 
• The uprising was primarily tribal in nature and did not evolve into a broader peasant movement.
 
 
 
• **Wahabi Movement**__
 __
 
• The **Wahabi Movement** was a religious reform movement inspired by the teachings of **Abdul Wahab** of Arabia.
 
• It aimed to purify Islam in India and advocated for the **removal of un-Islamic practices**.
 
• It had a strong anti-colonial character and was led by figures like **Syed Ahmed Barelvi**.
 
• However, it did not evolve into a peasant movement like the Farazi Movement.
 
 
 
• **Mappila Uprising**__
 
 
• The **Mappila Uprising** occurred in the **Malabar region** of Kerala and involved the **Mappila Muslims**.
 
• It was primarily a reaction against the oppressive policies of the British and the **exploitative landlords**.
 
• While it had a socio-economic aspect, it did not have the same religious reform roots as the Farazi Movement.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut is used to cut (move) text in MS Word?

• When you use this shortcut, the selected text is **removed from its current location** and stored in the **clipboard**.
 
• The **clipboard** is a temporary storage area where the cut or copied content is saved until it is pasted elsewhere.

• The **Ctrl + Z** shortcut is used to **undo the last action** performed in MS Word or other software.
 
• This command is helpful when you accidentally make changes and want to revert them quickly.

questions.question: What happens if you start a new blank presentation while another presentation is already open in MS PowerPoint?

options.text: A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.
MS PowerPoint displays an error message.
The slides from the current presentation are copied to the new one.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you start a new blank presentation in **MS PowerPoint** while another presentation is already open, it opens in a **new window.**
 
• This feature allows users to work on multiple presentations **simultaneously** without closing the current one.
 
• **MS PowerPoint** is designed to handle multiple windows, making it easier for users to copy content, compare slides, or work on different projects concurrently.
 
• Each presentation window operates independently, meaning changes in one presentation will not affect another unless content is explicitly copied and pasted.
 
• This functionality is useful in collaborative or multitasking environments where users may need to reference or edit multiple presentations.
 
• The ability to open multiple windows is a key feature of **Microsoft Office** applications, including PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MS PowerPoint Error Messages**__

 __
 
• Option 2 mentions an error message, but **MS PowerPoint** does not display an error when opening a new blank presentation alongside an existing one.
 
• Error messages are typically displayed in situations such as file corruption, compatibility issues, or software bugs.
 
 
 
• **Closing Presentations Automatically**__
 __
 
• Option 3 suggests that the current presentation closes automatically, which is incorrect as **MS PowerPoint** retains the current presentation when a new one is opened.
 
• This behavior ensures users do not lose unsaved work.
 
 
 
• **Copying Slides Automatically**__
 
 
• Option 4 suggests that slides are copied automatically from the current presentation to the new one, which is not a default feature.
 
• Slides can be copied manually by the user using the **copy-paste functionality** in PowerPoint.

__
 
• The **Daily Heart Rate Per Step (DHRPS)** is a smartwatch-based metric that tracks the relationship between an individual's heart rate and the number of steps taken daily.
 
• This metric was identified by researchers from **Northwestern University** in March 2025 as a useful predictor of **cardiovascular health risks.**
 
• The DHRPS provides insights into the **efficiency of the heart** during physical activity, helping to assess an individual's fitness levels.
 
• A higher DHRPS value may indicate potential **cardiovascular strain**, while lower values suggest better **cardiac efficiency**.
 
• This metric is particularly useful for individuals monitoring their **heart health** or engaging in fitness programs aimed at improving cardiovascular performance.
 
• The application of DHRPS can aid healthcare professionals in identifying at-risk patients and developing personalized health interventions.
